key_insight: AI scores become more clinically interpretable when paired with locally calibrated false discovery and false omission rates, not just a raw risk number.
clinical_relevance: For radiologists, showing FDR/FOR alongside an AI score may change recall behavior and increase confidence, especially at intermediate scores.
method: Estimated score-specific FDR and FOR for the Mirai mammography AI model across thresholds.
Used a retrospective screening mammography cohort of 130,712 exams to calculate locally calibrated error rates.
Ran a decision-making study with 21 radiologists comparing AI scores alone vs scores with FDR/FOR.
evidence_signal: Across thresholds, FDR and FOR varied widely, and in the reader study recall was lower when FDR/FOR were shown while confidence increased, especially at mid-range scores.
watch_item: These findings come from a single mammography model and reader study, so local calibration and workflow effects may not generalize to other sites, models, or imaging tasks.
paper_title: Locally calibrated error rates improve interpretability of AI scores and influence radiologist decision-making
